newsitem.title: INDIA: U.S. to take fresh look at India, Pakistan - envoy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to take fresh look at India, Pakistan - envoy.

text.p: The United States is prepared to take a fresh look at its policy towards India and Pakistan under President Bill Clinton's new administration, U.S. ambassador to India Frank Wisner said on Wednesday.
"We are beginning a new administration in Washington which will have a fresh look at the situation," Wisner told a news conference in Jammu, winter capital of India's Jammu and Kashmir state.
Indian newspapers recently reported that Secretary of State Madeleine Albright had indicated she took a keen interest in South Asia.
U.S. officials have said Assistant Secretary of State for South Asian Affairs Robin Raphel is expected to be replaced. Wisner has indicated he will probably leave New Delhi this year, diplomats said.
Wisner urged India and Pakistan to grasp the chance provided by the election of Nawaz Sharif as prime minister of Pakistan to resume peace talks that broke down three years ago.
"Pakistan has given this opportunity to India for a common ground, for a comprehensive dialogue between India and Pakistan for sorting out all bilateral issues including Kashmir," Wisner said.
India and Pakistan both stake a claim to the Himalayan region of Kashmir, which has been divided between the two countries since shortly after they won independence from Britain in 1947.
India controls two thirds of the region, which makes up part of Jammu and Kashmir state, while Pakistan rules over the remaining third.

New Delhi accuses Islamabad of arming guerrillas fighting against Indian rule in Jammu and Kashmir, where more than 20,000 people have died in insurgency-related violence since 1990. Pakistan says it provides only diplomatic support.
